articles.title: England v Pakistan: second men’s cricket Test, day four – live
articles.summary: Updates from day four at Lord’s; play starts 11am BST County cricket – live | Sign up for The Spin | Mail Tom. Here’s Ali Martin’s day three report: It was one of those days at Lord’s.
body: News from elsewhere: it’s been a frustrating, rain-flecked few days in the County Championship too, leaving all matches still live going into today’s final day, including an only-in-cricket close of play situation at Chester-le-Street, where Durham’s players went off for an early night (we trust) needing only four runs to polish off Gloucestershire. Tanya Aldred will be calling that match home, and all the others, through the day. Join her here.

It was one of those days at Lord’s. Rain meant just 24.5 overs were bowled and England’s already dominant position in this second Test meant overall jeopardy was in short supply. The spectators got a 50% refund but this only mildly offset their general frustration of following a sport that is so weather-dependent.

Yet for all this, it may in time prove a significant one for Dan Lawrence. During the two hours of play that were possible, and in hugely challenging conditions for the batters, Lawrence delivered an unbeaten 50 off 66 balls that cut through the gloom and showed his desire to make this latest stab at Test cricket count.

articles.title: Durham v Gloucestershire, Essex v Surrey, and more: county cricket, day four – live
articles.summary: Updates from the final day of this Championship round Day three roundup | Sign up for The Spin | Mail Tanya. Still showery everywhere except the southeast. The Met office says: Outbreaks of rain affect parts of Scotland and northern England at first.
body: There’s a damp patch just before the bowler’s delivery stride at the press box end. They’re hoping for play later dependent on sawdust and sun.

Rain rudely i nterrupted the County Championship on bank holiday Saturday but there was evening controversy at Chester-le-Street. Kasey Aldridge had bowled Durham to almost-victory with four for 47, giving him nine wickets in the match, leaving his side four to win. But with the floodlights on and filthy skies, Gloucestershire refused to bowl spin and the umpires said it was too dark for pace.

Mark Alleyne, the Gloucestershire head coach, explained: “Forty-five minutes before we lost the last wicket, it was too dark to play, which would have been consistent with all the other days that we played.

“I was really surprised that Carse was allowed to bowl to [James] Bracey at the time. He got him out, then took off straight away. So, yeah, we had probably 50 minutes of cricket there that we probably shouldn’t have done.

articles.title: Boreham Wood accept Vardy-beating record fee for Abdulmalik
articles.summary: Swedish club Djurgardens agree a National League record fee thought to be in excess of £1.5m to sign winger Abdul Abdulmalik from Boreham Wood.
body: The 23-year-old's move breaks the record fee paid for a fifth-tier player in England, set in 2012 when Leicester City paid Fleetwood Town £1m for Jamie Vardy.
Abdulmalik is currently in Sweden completing a medical after the deal was agreed on Sunday morning.

The forward enjoyed a breakthrough season in 2025-26, scoring 17 goals and providing 10 assists as Boreham Wood reached the National League play-off final, where he scored and set up a goal at Wembley.
The agreement also brings to an end a long-running transfer saga, with the Hertfordshire club having rejected bids of £1m and £1.5m for the former Millwall academy player earlier this summer.

articles.title: Emiliano Martínez finally gets his Villa exit with £7.5m move to Chelsea
articles.summary: Argentinian set to displace Sánchez as Blues’ No 1. ‘Coming to Chelsea was an easy decision to make’ Chelsea have completed the signing of Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez.
body: The 33-year-old, who has been agitating to leave Villa for the last two summers, has finally got his wish as he has moved for £7.5m, signing a three-year contract at Stamford Bridge. Martínez, who won the 2022 World Cup with Argentina and twice secured the Yashin Trophy for the best goalkeeper, is set to displace Robert Sánchez as Chelsea’s No 1 goalkeeper.

“I’m delighted to be at this football club,” Martinez told their official website. “Coming to Chelsea, for me and my family, was an easy decision to make and I’m just over the moon – I can’t wait to get started. I want to be successful here. I’m someone who wants to win at everything I do and I want to bring that here to this football club because it’s a football club that wins titles, so I think it’s a good match.
“I’m all passion and I play with my heart. I will give 100% every game, every training session to make the club, my teammates and the supporters proud.”

articles.title: ‘I’ve had a very hectic career’: Mario Balotelli on Italian football’s troubles and his future
articles.summary: Striker talks life in the UAE, problems with the Azzurri and ‘special feeling’ of playing for Manchester City. Whenever the name Mario Balotelli is brought up, particularly in Italy, the conversation is almost inevitably laced with a sense of regret.
body: Yet being in front of him, with a smile on his face, it becomes clear the 36-year-old striker has reached an unexpected level of wisdom and maturity, traits that shine through in his lucid analysis of Italian football’s current struggles and the vanishing street culture of the sport. As Balotelli reflects on what he would tell his adolescent self, there is also a distinct feeling that he has finally made peace with his own turbulent narrative, that he isn’t chasing the ghosts of unfulfilled expectations.

Balotelli joined Al Ittifaq in the United Arab Emirates simply to enjoy the game, to find pure joy on the pitch, and to realise a long-held family dream of playing alongside his brother, Enock Barwuah. “To tell you the truth, it was an idea that came up more or less at the last minute,” he says. “The president wanted to meet me, and we talked. The project interested me. Everyone always says: ‘You go to Dubai for the money,’ but thank God, I’m not short of that. So, money wasn’t the only goal. The project was actually nice and competitive. I grew fond of the idea and decided to give it a try.”

articles.title: Everton call off Armstrong sale after fan backlash
articles.summary: Everton have called off a proposed deal to sell midfielder Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest following a backlash from the club's supporters.
body: Forest made a bid of £40m plus a potential sell-on clause for the England Under-19 international, who is regarded as one of the brightest prospects to emerge from Finch Farm in recent years.
The news enraged Everton supporters, who sang Armstrong's name throughout Saturday's draw at Bournemouth and said there would be a "riot" if he was sold.
The Toffees board have now unanimously decided that the 19-year-old will remain at Hill Dickinson Stadium.
Armstrong has made 24 appearances for Everton and played 87 minutes against the Cherries before he was replaced by Charly Alcaraz.

articles.title: Leverkusen U-Turn: Robert Andrich now expected to stay
articles.summary: Robert Andrich’s future at Bayer Leverkusen has taken a surprising turn. The 31-year-old midfielder had recently emerged as a clear candidate to leave the club after new head coach Carles Martínez made it clear that Andrich would initially have only a minor role in his midfield plans.
body: However, just days before the transfer window closes, a U-turn now appears to be underway.
Following Bayer’s surprising 3-2 defeat at newly promoted SV Elversberg on Saturday, sporting CEO Simon Rolfes indicated that he expects Andrich to stay.
“I assume that he will stay,” Rolfes said after the disappointing Bundesliga opener.

Andrich still has a contract with Leverkusen until 2028, but his position within the squad had changed significantly this summer. Martínez stripped him of the captaincy, with Edmond Tapsoba taking over, and made no secret of the fact that the experienced midfielder was currently behind several competitors.

articles.title: US Open key questions: Is Alcaraz fit? Will Sabalenka make history?
articles.summary: The US Open, of all the four slams, is notoriously the hardest to predict the winners of as it falls at a time of year when eight months into the season the players are more likely than not nursing aches and pains with their bodies battered from the grind of the tour.
body: It's also played on a surface where more players fancy their chances; many have love-hate relationships with clay and grass but hard courts are their bread and butter.

The US Open is now a three-week event, week one is fan week, which this year saw five-time champion Roger Federer return for an exhibition, Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik win their first Grand Slam title after being crowned mixed doubles champions - in a competition that saw a return to Flushing Meadows of six-time champion Serena Williams - and the qualifying competition, which started with 15 Brits in the draw.

The main draw starts on Sunday and contains nine Brits, with a record five coming through qualifying. The men's competition is headed up by Sascha Zverev in the absence of Jannik Sinner [knee injury] and the women's by world No 1 Aryna Sabalenka.

If we break down the draws starting with the men, the top half is headed up in the absence of Sinner by Zverev, top seed at a Grand Slam for the first time and with a major title under his belt having won the French Open earlier this year.

articles.title: Real Madrid will not take any risks with key midfielder; expected to get minutes from Rayo Vallecano clash
articles.summary: According to AS, Real Madrid have no intention of rushing key midfielder Aurelien Tchouameni back from the sidelines. The priority is for him to return at 100% fitness rather than take unnecessary risks. That is manager Jose Mourinho’s approach with the French midfielder.
body: Tchoaumeni suffered an injury during the World Cup that forced him to miss two matches in the final stages before returning for the semi-final. That situation aggravated the problem and prevented him from training at the same pace as his teammates.
After missing all of Real Madrid’s preseason friendlies, Mourinho has no intention of taking risks at this stage of the campaign.
He is a key part of the manager’s plans, which is precisely why the Portuguese coach would rather give him the necessary time to regain his fitness than push him too early.
“With Tchouameni, we have to keep our emotions in check. I don’t want him to be in and out, in and out again,” Mourinho said at the press conference ahead of the Malaga game.

articles.title: Norris: I can be forceful to get what I want at McLaren
articles.summary: Reigning world champion Lando Norris says he is in a position at McLaren where he "can be forceful to try to get what I want" after signing a contract extension with the team.
body: Norris claimed his maiden title in 2025 to become McLaren's first world championship winner since Lewis Hamilton triumphed for them in 2008.

Having emerged victorious in an intense season-long title battle with his team-mate Oscar Piastri, Norris has further enhanced his status within the Woking squad by clearly outperforming the Australian so far in 2026.

The 26-year-old Brit's position at the centre of the team's future was cemented on Saturday when he signed a contract extension to stay with McLaren until at least the end of 2030, with a multi-year option to potentially extend further beyond that included in the deal.
Asked during an exclusive interview with Sky Sports News about how his role within the team has changed over time, Norris said: "You learn over the years when you should talk, when you shouldn't.

articles.title: Fery's dreams of maiden ATP Tour title ended in Winston-Salem Open final
articles.summary: Arthur Fery's hopes of landing his maiden ATP Tour title at Winston-Salem Open was ended in emphatic fashion by Peruvian Ignacio Buse on Saturday.
body: From 3-3 in the first set, Fery lost six straight games before eventually going down 6-3 6-2 to Buse.
The promising 22-year-old clinched his second trophy of the season having lifted his maiden tour-level trophy at the ATP 500 event in Hamburg.
Fery was aiming to add to his already memorable season having reached the semi-finals at Wimbledon and he is set for a new career high Monday.
With his spot in the Winston-Salem final, 24-year-old Fery has moved up to a new career high of No 33 in the live rankings, overtaking Cameron Norrie as the British No 1 in doing so.
